# Skill project manifest for skill-publisher.
#
# What this declares: the units an agent working IN THIS CHECKOUT needs.
# This repository IS the authoring authority itself, which makes its manifest the
# shortest of the fleet: there is no separate unit to consult about how to write a
# SKILL.md, because that is what the tracked files here ARE. The working tree is
# the authority, and the one unit it genuinely needs is the one it documents.
#
# It deliberately does NOT declare `skill-publisher` itself. This repository IS that
# unit's source of truth; installing it into its own home would give an agent two
# copies of one unit with no rule about which one it is editing, and would make
# the checkout's own edits invisible until a publish round trip.
#
# How the home is produced — read this before running `project resolve`
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
# `project resolve` writes into whatever `SKILL_MANAGER_HOME` names. Run it
# before this checkout has its own home and it mutates the operator's global
# ~/.skill-manager. Create the local home first, point `SKILL_MANAGER_HOME` at
# it, and only then resolve:
#
#   mkdir -p .skill-manager/skills
#   SKILL_MANAGER_CLI=<epic skill-manager> \
#     bash <git-integration-repo>/scripts/bootstrap-home.sh --root "$PWD" --force
#   export SKILL_MANAGER_HOME="$PWD/.skill-manager"
#   export CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR="$PWD/.claude"  CLAUDE_HOME="$PWD/.claude"
#   export CODEX_HOME="$PWD/.codex"          GEMINI_HOME="$PWD/.gemini"
#   skill-manager project resolve --project-dir "$PWD" --skip-gateway \
#     --allow-same-home
#
# Two things in that sequence are not optional, and each was a real failure:
#
#   * The four agent-home vars. `SKILL_MANAGER_HOME` alone does NOT redirect the
#     agent-home projections — set only that and `resolve` symlinks this
#     project's units into the operator's real ~/.claude, ~/.codex and ~/.gemini.
#     These are the paths `home describe --json`'s `env` block names and the
#     launch shims under `.skill-manager/bin/launch/` export for you, which is
#     why launching through a shim is the supported way in.
#
#   * `--allow-same-home`. This project's home IS its own parent home — there is
#     no tier between ~/.skill-manager and here — and `project resolve` refuses
#     that layout by default (skill-manager #32) because it "isolates nothing".
#     The refusal is a doctrine guard, not a data-loss guard: ChildHomeMaterializer's
#     three degenerate-layout guards already decline a same-tree materialization.
#     The only alternative is to point SKILL_MANAGER_HOME at the operator's
#     global home, which would write it, and that is forbidden.
#
# Expect `resolve` to need SEVERAL passes: it validates markdown `skill-imports`
# against INSTALLED units, not declared ones, so a unit whose imports name a unit
# installed later in the same run fails the first pass and succeeds on the next.
#
# Coords are git-only (no registry is configured) and they name the REPO, not the
# installed unit — see skill-publisher's references/coords-and-distribution.md.
# The table key is the installed unit name, which is what
# `.skill-manager/skills/<name>` uses.

[project]
name = "skill-publisher"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Author and maintain installable skill-manager units: skills, plugins, doc-repos and harnesses, and ship edits into a store via commit, push and sync."

# --- subject matter AND a declared markdown import. This unit's SKILL.md
#     `skill-imports` names skill-manager references/skill-imports.md, and
#     `project resolve` validates markdown imports against INSTALLED units, so
#     leaving it undeclared fails the whole resolve with "references missing
#     unit". Substantively: every claim this skill makes about install, bind,
#     sync, instantiate, coords, CLI deps and MCP deps is a claim about
#     skill-manager's behavior, so it is the thing to check a change against ---

[skills.skill-manager]
source = "github:haydenrear/skill-manager-skill"

# --- no [[vendored]] block: this repo tracks no symlinks and has no test_graph,
#     so no path in the working tree holds content owned by another unit.
#     Verified with `git ls-files -s | grep ^120000` -> 0 entries, before and
#     after onboarding. Nothing to migrate, nothing to validate.
